avoid_supplements.name: Calcium supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Calcium and iron compete for absorption in the GI tract; concurrent use reduces iron bioavailability by 20-50%
avoid_supplements.action: Separate administration by at least 2 hours; take iron on empty stomach when possible

avoid_supplements.name: Zinc supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Both metals compete for intestinal absorption; can reduce iron absorption and impair zinc status
avoid_supplements.action: Separate by 2+ hours; monitor serum iron and zinc levels if concurrent use necessary

avoid_supplements.name: Polyphenol/Tannin-containing supplements (green tea, black tea extracts)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Polyphenols and tannins form insoluble complexes with iron, drastically reducing absorption
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent ingestion; separate by at least 2 hours

avoid_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Mg competes with Fe for absorption in the proximal small intestine
avoid_supplements.action: Stagger doses by 2+ hours; prioritize iron absorption timing

avoid_supplements.name: Phosphate binders (calcium phosphate, aluminum hydroxide)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Form insoluble iron complexes in the GI lumen, preventing absorption

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin E (high-dose >400 IU)
caution_supplements.mechanism: High-dose vitamin E may impair iron absorption through mild antioxidant interference
caution_supplements.action: Monitor hemoglobin/ferritin; use standard doses only

caution_supplements.name: Copper supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Iron and copper compete for absorption; high iron may reduce copper status over time
caution_supplements.action: Monitor copper levels with long-term concurrent use; space dosing if possible

avoid_foods.name: Tea (black, green, white)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Tannins and polyphenols in tea form insoluble complexes with iron, reducing absorption by up to 50-70%
avoid_foods.action: Avoid tea consumption within 2 hours before and after iron dosing

avoid_foods.name: Coffee
avoid_foods.mechanism: Chlorogenic acid and polyphenols in coffee chelate iron, reducing bioavailability
avoid_foods.action: Separate coffee and iron administration by at least 2 hours

avoid_foods.name: Dairy products (milk, cheese, yogurt)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Calcium and phosphates in dairy form poorly absorbable iron complexes
avoid_foods.action: Take iron on empty stomach, away from dairy; wait 2+ hours between doses

avoid_foods.name: High-fiber foods (bran, whole grains, legumes)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Phytates and fiber in whole grains/legumes bind iron and reduce absorption
avoid_foods.action: Take iron 1-2 hours before or 4+ hours after high-fiber meals

avoid_foods.name: Spinach, kale, and leafy greens
avoid_foods.mechanism: Oxalates in spinach form insoluble complexes with iron; 'heme-iron myth' makes non-heme supplemental iron particularly vulnerable
avoid_foods.action: Avoid concurrent consumption; separate by 2+ hours for optimal absorption

avoid_foods.name: Nuts and seeds
avoid_foods.mechanism: Phytates and mineral compounds in nuts/seeds inhibit iron absorption
avoid_foods.action: Take iron away from nut/seed consumption; separate by 2+ hours

caution_foods.name: Citrus fruits (orange, lemon, grapefruit)
caution_foods.mechanism: Vitamin C and citric acid enhance iron absorption; this is actually beneficial but may increase GI side effects
caution_foods.action: Can take with iron to enhance absorption, but monitor for GI upset; may reduce nausea if taken together

caution_foods.name: Red meat and poultry
caution_foods.mechanism: Heme iron from meat may compete with non-heme supplemental iron for absorption pathways; minimal clinical impact
caution_foods.action: No restriction needed; may consume together, though heme/non-heme absorption is independent

caution_foods.name: Eggs
caution_foods.mechanism: Eggs contain phosphoproteins that weakly bind iron; minor effect on non-heme iron absorption
caution_foods.action: Space administration by 1-2 hours for optimal absorption if concerned

monitoring_notes: Ferrous sulfate absorption is critically dependent on gastric pH and timing relative to chelating agents (polyphenols, tannins, calcium, phosphates). Patients should take iron on an empty stomach 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals/supplements for maximal bioavailability. Monitor serum ferritin, hemoglobin, and transferrin saturation every 4-8 weeks during therapy; counsel patients on GI side effects and the importance of strict timing separation from interacting substances.
